name: ARO-ALK7

lead: ARO-ALK7 is an experimental RNA interference drug directed at ALK7, a receptor involved in fat-cell signalling. Fat-loss followers discuss it as a possible non-appetite route to losing body fat.

RNAi lowers production of a chosen protein by silencing its gene. The chain is less ALK7 signalling, fat cells releasing more stored fat, then fat loss and a leaner look. The only public record is a phase 1/2 first-in-human study that began on 9 May 2025 and plans to enroll 150 adults; no results have been reported.

paras: It is available only in the clinical trial, in adults with obesity with and without type 2 diabetes.
No safety data have been reported. It is investigational and not available by prescription.

lead: ARO-ALK7 is an investigational RNA interference (RNAi) therapy directed at ALK7, a receptor involved in fat-cell signalling. It is being tested in adults with obesity, with and without type 2 diabetes. It is not approved for any use.[1]

The sole source of public information is a clinical trial registration: a Phase 1/2 first-in-human study (NCT06937203) that began on 9 May 2025, is recruiting, and plans to enroll 150 adults.[1] No results have been reported in the sources reviewed.
